item.title: How to Compare Value: Price-per-Milligram THC on Edibles

item.description: When a 22-year-old in San Jose shops legally, parents still have questions. Curiosity beats catastrophe scripts, and boundaries still matter.

item.description: Cannabis wedding favors photograph beautifully and create real legal risk when hosts improvise sales, underage guests, or public consumption.

item.description: Adults 21+ may give limited amounts to other adults without compensation. The awkward part is everything people try to bolt onto that sentence.

item.title: Holiday Hosting from Labor Day to Halloween: Shop the Calendar Smartly
item.description: Late-summer barbecues slide into spooky-season hangs. A shopping calendar keeps hosts legal, stocked, and out of edible-chaos stories.

item.title: Growing at Home in San Jose: Plant Limits and Neighbor Smell Fights
item.description: State law caps personal grows at six living plants per residence, with local rules layered on top. Odor fights are where many South Bay home grows actually break.

item.description: Purple Lotus listed Labor Day deals for Sept. 4–7, 2026, with both San Jose doors on the event page. Read the brand table, tax math, and ID rules before you chase percentages.

item.title: Pet Safety: Edibles Look Like Treats, and San Jose Households Need a Plan
item.description: Gummies, chocolates, and baked goods confuse pets as easily as toddlers. California agencies point owners to Animal Poison Control, and to locked storage.

item.title: What to Do If You Feel Over-Intoxicated: Edible Safety for San Jose Adults
item.description: Edibles hit later and harder than many first-timers expect. California Poison Control and CDPH guidance beat internet myths when a dose goes sideways.

item.title: Porch Theft and Delivery Security in San Jose Neighborhoods
item.description: Legal cannabis delivery still ends at a front door. Neighborhood porch pirates and cash-heavy habits make timing, verification, and stash discipline part of shopper safety.

item.title: Shopping with a Friend or Caretaker: Etiquette and Consent
item.description: Bringing support to the counter helps, if roles, privacy, and consent stay clear for everyone in the vestibule.

item.title: Accessibility: Mobility and Sensory-Friendly Shopping Tips
item.description: Scarce storefronts and industrial addresses can be hard to navigate. A little planning makes licensed retail usable for more bodies and brains.

item.title: Sharks, Earthquakes, 49ers Watch Energy: Hosting Without Breaking House Rules
item.description: Game-day hosting is a San Jose art. Cannabis can be part of an adult living room, never a parking-lot plan outside SAP Center or Levi’s Stadium.

item.title: Mexican, Vietnamese, and South Bay Flavors with Cannabis Hospitality Nights
item.description: East Side and Story Road foodways meet adult cannabis hospitality, without collapsing culture into a stereotype or a public smoke session.

item.description: Munchies are culture, not a dosing strategy. Pair sealed product with South Bay food habits, and keep the feast private.

item.title: Smoke vs. Vapor vs. Edibles Near Apartments and HOAs
item.description: Lease clauses and neighbor shared air beat strain preferences, edibles and sealed storage avoid most smoke fights.

item.description: Private property rules still govern, most hotels ban smoking, and hosts can forbid cannabis even when California allows adult use.

item.title: Flying Out of SJC with Cannabis (Spoiler: Don’t)
item.description: State-legal jars do not clear federal airport screening, leave cannabis out of Norman Y. Mineta San Jose International.

item.description: Sealed packages or the trunk, open flower on the seat is how a legal purchase becomes a ticket.

item.title: How Far Can Legal Cannabis Delivery Go in the South Bay?
item.description: City registration and destination rules, not app radius maps, decide whether a van can lawfully stop at your door.

item.description: Only city-registered operators with completed registration may deliver, apps and unmarked vans do not rewrite that rule.

item.title: Returns, Recalls, and What to Do When a Product Fails You
item.description: Licensed cannabis is not always returnable like a sweater, but recalls, complaints, and batch IDs give shoppers a path.

item.title: Debit, Cash, and ATMs: Paying for Cannabis in San Jose
item.description: Federal banking friction still shapes the counter, cash and cashless ATM debit remain the everyday toolkit.

item.description: A deal board is not a blank check, ask what stacks, what is pre-tax, and what the register will actually honor.

item.description: Tipping is generally allowed and appreciated, but it is etiquette, not a substitute for wages or a workaround for discounts.

item.description: The door check is not theater, California pairs hard age gates with daily retail weight caps.

item.description: Age gates, daily purchase limits, and paperwork differ, public consumption rules mostly do not.
